title: Small apartment design: 10 storage and space ideas
seo_title: Small Apartment Design: 10 Storage and Space Ideas
description: Small apartment design: floor-to-ceiling wardrobes, hidden doors, niches, concealed lighting, convertible furniture. 10 storage ideas, mistakes, checklist.
lead: In a small apartment every centimetre counts. Small apartment design is above all well-planned storage, so we have gathered the solutions we use most often to give everything its place while keeping the space light.
photo_alt: Living room — Linden Penthouse, a CAS Development project
body: h2
Start with the layout
p

The biggest effect comes not from decor but from the right layout: where the walk-in wardrobe goes, how the doors open, how much space the passage takes. That is why a design project starts with furniture-layout options.
p

In a small apartment the layout decides whether there will be room for storage at all. Sometimes it is enough to shift a partition, swap hinged doors for sliding ones or merge the hallway with a wardrobe area — and a full-size wardrobe appears where there was none before.
h2
10 storage and space ideas
ol
Floor-to-ceiling wardrobes: the top shelves are for seasonal items.
Fronts in the wall colour and hidden doors — the wardrobe “disappears”.
Niches in walls and partitions for shelves and appliances.
A bed with a lift-up mechanism and drawers.
A built-in washer and dryer stacked in a column in the bathroom or hallway.
Wall-hung vanity units and a concealed-cistern toilet — the floor stays clear and cleaning is easier.
Mirrors and glass to visually double the space.
Concealed linear lighting instead of bulky chandeliers.
A kitchen island or breakfast bar that works as both a table and storage.
One calm colour and a minimum of different materials.
p

None of these ideas on its own will turn a cramped apartment into a spacious one. The effect comes from the combination: floor-to-ceiling wardrobes free the room from chests of drawers, lighting makes them look light, and a single colour for fronts and walls removes visual noise. That is why we build storage into the layout from the start rather than adding wardrobes after the renovation.

h2
How to make the space feel bigger
p

Storage is only half the job. The other half is making sure the apartment does not look cluttered. Simple techniques work here: the same flooring in every room without thresholds, full-height doors, light matt handleless fronts and a minimum of open shelving. Light is better spread around the room — lighting in niches, under cabinets and along the ceiling makes the space feel deeper than a single central chandelier.
p
Do not be afraid of dark accents either: one dark wall or deep-coloured fronts in a niche can add depth if the rest of the space is light.
p
It is also worth reducing the number of free-standing pieces. A built-in floor-to-ceiling wardrobe reads as a wall, while three separate chests of drawers look like a storeroom.
h2
Made-to-measure furniture: where it pays off most
ul
hallway — a wardrobe with room for shoes, outerwear and the vacuum cleaner
kitchen — wall cabinets up to the ceiling, drawers instead of hinged doors
bedroom — a bed with drawers and a wardrobe in a niche or along the whole wall
bathroom — a tall unit for the washing machine and a wall-hung vanity
living room — a TV wall with closed storage and hidden cabling
p

Drawings for made-to-measure furniture are part of the design project: heights, depths, wardrobe interiors, socket and lighting positions. The joiner builds to the finished dimensions, and the electrician brings power in advance to wherever it is needed.

h2
Common mistakes in small apartment design
ul
buying ready-made furniture before the layout is fixed
stopping wardrobes short of the ceiling and leaving a dust-collecting gap above
mixing many different materials and colours in a small area
forgetting sockets inside cabinets for appliances and chargers
leaving one chandelier as the only light source
p
Most of these mistakes are expensive to fix after the renovation, so it is worth catching them on paper — in the layout and drawings.
h2
Checklist before the renovation starts
ul
list everything that needs storing: clothes, appliances, sports gear, seasonal items
decide where the washing machine, vacuum cleaner and dryer will go
sign off the layout before the electrical work starts
put made-to-measure furniture dimensions into the drawings before the finishing works
plan lighting scenes together with wardrobes and niches

faq: Should the kitchen be combined with the living room?
Often yes: the space becomes brighter. But you need a powerful extractor hood and well-thought-out zoning.
In a small apartment, built-in made-to-measure furniture is usually the better deal: it uses every centimetre.
Which colours work best for a small apartment?
Calm light shades and minimal contrast; it is better to add an accent with one object or textiles than with a different wall colour in every room.
Where to store things if there is no walk-in wardrobe?
In built-in floor-to-ceiling wardrobes, in a bed with a lift-up mechanism, in niches and under window sills — we look for storage space at the layout stage.
